subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should this issue be resolved by documenting HTTP Request URLs as the preferred low-latency hosted Slack transport, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and the remaining measured delay is mostly before OpenClaw code runs, but steering users or changing defaults affects Slack setup expectations and deployment requirements.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local and firewalled deployments, and make the Slack docs/setup guidance explicitly prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Have maintainers sponsor a stronger setup or default change that steers new hosted Slack installs away from Socket Mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Decide the current transport table is sufficient and close only after recording that no additional latency-specific docs or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local and firewalled deployments, and make the Slack docs/setup guidance explicitly prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the measurement, landed the current-main partial Slack fix, and scoped the remaining follow-up to HTTP mode guidance.
